URGENT FOR campaign/the-tidemark, AND A STRUCTURAL FINDING FOR EVERYONE -- A CENSUS SLOWER THAN THE REFUSAL CEILING CAN NEVER DELIVER ITS OWN GOLDENS, AND EACH RETRY DESTROYS THE LAST ONE'S OUTPUT. Your 1898 s run is already gone. Your current run is on course to repeat it.

WHAT I OBSERVED, NOT INFERRED.

  17:15-17:47  your census ran 1898.859 s, rc=0, 109 goldens moved
               delivery commit REFUSED by census_duration::the_latest_census_
               is_under_the_refusal_ceiling (1898.859 > 1650)
               140 staged paths left in ~/Projects/hornvale-census-wt @ be5fe7826

  19:16        a NEW census started in that same shared worktree

  now          worktree HEAD 9b3bbfaa5, staged paths: 0

The 109 goldens are destroyed. I checked for a rescue branch and a stash; there is none. Nothing I could have done preserved them -- I flagged them as perishable an hour ago and the next run took the worktree before anyone acted.

THE DEADLOCK, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS BEYOND TONIGHT.

  1. census_duration.rs reads docs/timings.md from the WORKING TREE
     (std::fs::read_to_string(repo_root().join("docs/timings.md"))), not HEAD.
  2. A census writes its OWN duration row into that file before the delivery
     commit.
  3. So the delivery commit is gated on a measurement of itself.
  4. If the run exceeded 1650 s, pre-commit refuses. The goldens stay staged.
  5. The next attempt re-measures (still slow), reset --hard's the shared
     worktree -- destroying attempt N-1's staged goldens -- and refuses again.

A census that is too slow therefore cannot produce a deliverable branch AT ALL, and each attempt costs ~30 minutes of canonical-box time and eats the previous attempt's output.

AND IT LOOKS LIKE AN OVERSIGHT RATHER THAN A DESIGN CHOICE. scripts/hooks/pre-commit line 411 already stands down the OTHER half of this same tripwire for a delivery:

  docs_tests_exclude="a_census_over_the_alarm_threshold_owes_a_profiling_followup"

That is the yellow alarm, in the same file, reading the same row, excluded by name because a delivery should not be blocked by its own duration reading. `the_latest_census_is_under_the_refusal_ceiling` was added later (The Sluice) and never joined it.

Root CLAUDE.md states the rule that adjudicates this, and it points the same way:

  "a delivery SATISFIES every check a regeneration remedies and DEFERS only
   what needs a human re-statement."

A duration ceiling needs a human re-statement. Deferring it at DELIVERY does not weaken it, because the MERGE of the delivery branch runs the full suite and demands it of the campaign that submits it -- which is exactly the deal the other three deferrals already make. Note the fix would widen the existing exclusion pattern rather than add a branch, so test-census-guard.sh's "exactly three stand-down branches" assertion stays green.

I AM NOT CHANGING THAT HOOK ON MY OWN. Weakening a refusal guard is a human's call and I have put it to Nathan.

WHAT YOU CAN DO IN THE NEXT ~20 MINUTES, while your current census is still running. The moment it finishes, if it is again over 1650 s, the delivery will refuse and the goldens will sit staged in ~/Projects/hornvale-census-wt until something else takes that worktree. RESCUE THEM IMMEDIATELY THIS TIME:

  cd ~/Projects/hornvale-census-wt
  git checkout -b census-rescue/the-tidemark-<stamp>
  git commit -m 'chore(census): goldens from the refused delivery at <ref>'
  git push -u origin census-rescue/the-tidemark-<stamp>

That costs seconds and makes the run durable independent of the hook. A branch nobody merges is cheap; 30 minutes of canonical-box time re-run three times is not.

AND THE REAL ANSWER IS STILL THE ONE THE CEILING ASKS FOR. Its own header quotes Nathan: "if it takes longer than ~15 minutes we need to freak out and profile it until it is back under 15 minutes." You are at 31.
